readout: Phosphotransferase activity inferred from yeast growth, as the deposit's activity_score; higher is more active
assay_method: NNK mutagenesis of two regions of human Src -- the catalytic domain and the SH4 domain -- assayed in yeast, where Src kinase activity is growth-inhibitory. Variants were barcoded and the barcode-variant map determined by subassembly; plasmid barcodes were sequenced at three OD-defined timepoints on an Illumina NextSeq. Per-variant scores were taken from the authors' MaveDB deposit, using its activity_score column, which inverts the growth score so that higher means more active.
remark: The sequence is full-length UniProt P12931, 536 aa, and both of the deposit's score sets are renumbered onto it: the catalytic-domain set is numbered 1-250 against a 250-residue excerpt that is P12931 270-519 verbatim, so +269, and the SH4 set is numbered 1-18 from the residue after the initiator Met, which is cleaved for myristoylation, so +1. After those offsets bad = 0 on both. MaveDB gives both sets the same target record, 'Src catalytic domain', which is wrong for the SH4 set and is what made a pooled label check fail. The two sets are one work item and are joined: same protein, same assay, same quantity, two library regions. They share no variant, so the merge rests on the dead-variant anchor, and that anchor holds -- nonsense medians of -1.606 and -1.639. The readout is the deposit's activity_score, not its score. Active Src is toxic to yeast, so the growth-derived score runs backwards: under it the 152 nonsense variants, which are dead kinase, sat above the substitutions. activity_score is exactly -score on all 3,866 rows and puts them below, which is the direction a dead kinase must take. Those nonsense rows are then dropped, a premature stop not being writable as a substitution. There is no wild-type row in either set, so wt_readout is empty and the zero point of normalized-score is the dataset mean.
